title: Vancouver Goldeneyes GM Cara Gardner Morey steps down to coach
dek: Cara Gardner Morey, the Vancouver Goldeneyes' general manager, has stepped down from her front-office role to become the team's head coach after one inaugural season. The PWHL will oversee a search for her replacement at GM.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Cara Gardner Morey transitioned from GM to head coach of the Vancouver Goldeneyes after the team's first season, citing her return to coaching as her primary strength.
bottom_line: Watch who the PWHL appoints as interim or permanent GM and whether they retain Gardner Morey's draft picks and roster philosophy. The speed of the GM search and any public disagreements between front office and coaching will signal whether this transition stabilizes or destabilizes the franchise heading into Year Two.
body: Cara Gardner Morey, the Vancouver Goldeneyes' general manager and architect of the franchise's inaugural roster, has stepped down from the front office to become the team's head coach, the PWHL announced.

Gardner Morey, 47, spent the past year building the Goldeneyes from scratch in the PWHL's first season. The franchise was the first team eliminated from playoff contention. Coach Brian Idalski was fired following that playoff elimination, opening the head coaching vacancy that Gardner Morey will now fill.

Gardner Morey brings 14 seasons of NCAA Division I head-coaching experience from her tenure at Princeton, where she compiled a program-record 26-win season in 2020 and led the team to their first ECAC tournament title that year. In an on-the-record statement, she said, "I realized how much I missed being behind the bench," and noted that "coaching is where I know I can make the biggest impact."

The transition leaves the Goldeneyes without a GM while the PWHL oversees a search for Gardner Morey's replacement. No interim GM or timeline for the search has been announced. The team completed last month's draft with the No. 1 overall pick, selecting U.S. Olympic team defender Caroline Harvey.

Gardner Morey's shift from front office to bench tests whether her college-coaching record and direct influence over day-to-day player development can turn around a franchise that failed to reach the postseason in Year One.
